A CLEARER PICTURE

Your practice is personal.
Your security should be practical.

A booking platform, an email account, a shared document. Everyday tools form an important part of your practice.

The proposed Cyber Defender review brings those dependencies into focus. It separates verified observations from questions that need checking, then turns the findings into an achievable action plan.

Using a supplier is not evidence of a weakness. We focus on what the evidence supports and where a closer, authorised assessment would be useful.

STRAIGHT ANSWERS

Before we
begin.

Will you need access to client records?

An initial review should not require clinical notes or identifiable client information. Any later access must be justified, minimised and covered by an agreed scope and appropriate safeguards.

Does using a particular supplier mean we are vulnerable?

No. A supplier’s historic incident or its presence on your website does not establish a current vulnerability at your practice. Findings need relevant, current evidence.

Is this a penetration test?

Not by default. A baseline review is different from intrusive testing. Any specialist testing would need separate written authorisation, clear boundaries and qualified personnel.

Will this replace our existing IT provider?

The proposed approach is collaborative. An independent review can help clarify priorities and responsibilities alongside your existing support.

Can you certify us as fully secure or compliant?

No. A review is a time-limited assessment, not a guarantee of security or legal compliance. Any certification or legal advice requires a suitably qualified provider and a defined process.
